body:
> ## ⚠ AMENDED 2026-10-19 — read this first
>
> **Status retained: `ENTRY_GATE_FAILED — SCORER_NOT_QUALIFIED`.** No production
> CPR training, no development operating-point selection, no held-out comparison
> and no CPR-versus-control result exists. **CPR improvement remains untested.**
>
> **The original body below repeats claims that are now withdrawn.** Corrections
> are in
> [`AMENDMENT_01_GATE_FIDELITY_AND_ACCOUNTING.md`](https://github.com/bijay299/XXResearch/blob/5c2d99516164eae426358d7a390191cc184079bb/results/cpr_real_model_controls_v1/AMENDMENT_01_GATE_FIDELITY_AND_ACCOUNTING.md),
> which governs. In particular:
>
> * **"All ten errors are false positives" is wrong.** The 32 negative
>   references are **22 absent, 6 present, 4 uncertain** — six definite false
>   positives plus four uncertain decisions.
> * **Per-probe values are observed correct-negative fractions**, not
>   specificities, and **no object is independently qualified** (8–16 positives
>   and 10–11 negatives each, against a ≥20/≥20 requirement). "bicycle 0.909 /
>   violin 0.900 would have cleared the gate" is withdrawn.
> * **Softmax outputs are single deterministic decisions, not probabilities**;
>   3/11 is a count across eleven images, not a per-image frequency.
> * **Weak negation handling is a plausible explanation, not a proven cause**,
>   and nothing here shows CLIP generally cannot measure presence.
> * **"No training of any kind" would be wrong:** three native bring-up training
>   segments ran (22 processed timesteps, 2 optimizer updates each).
> * **Accounting and retry claims are corrected:** the one-technical-retry cap
>   was **breached** (8 bring-up launches = 7 relaunches); final counters are
>   0.1198536 GPU-h / 0.1276836 CPU-core-h with lower bounds ≥0.1515586 /
>   ≥0.1651622 h; the evaluation reserve was **not** untouched.
>
> Assets, their IDs, bytes, digests and the tag target are **unchanged**. This
> notice is the only release metadata change.

# CPR real-model controls pilot v1 — entry-gate artifacts

**Terminal status: `ENTRY_GATE_FAILED — SCORER_NOT_QUALIFIED`**

Scientific work stopped at the integrated entry gate. **No production training
ran; no development matrix, no held-out matrix and no arm comparison exist**, so
no scientific decision (`PROMISING_FOR_FRESH_REPLICATION`,
`NO_ADVANTAGE_DEMONSTRATED`, `INCONCLUSIVE`) is available or claimed.

The frozen object-presence scorer reached **sensitivity 1.000 (32/32)** but
**specificity 0.6875 (22/32)**, below the required 0.80. All ten errors are
false positives and eight are the **`backpack`** probe — **specificity 0.273**,
versus bicycle 0.909 and violin 0.900. `backpack` is the development target, so
the selection stage and everything downstream was unmeasurable. Per contract,
failed qualification ends the task: no scorer shopping, no threshold retuning.

Report: [`results/cpr_real_model_controls_v1/FINAL_REPORT.md`](https://github.com/bijay299/XXResearch/blob/a462b94800d44441c6c056c4cd220350862741ad/results/cpr_real_model_controls_v1/FINAL_REPORT.md)

| `m0_dev_images.tar.gz` | the 1 declared M0 development case decoded during bring-up |
| `entry_gate_bringup_probe_adapter.pt` | 28.55 MiB compact LoRA adapter from the bring-up timing probe (22 processed timesteps). **Entry-gate artifact evidencing the save/reload proof — not a trained erasure model.** |

# CPR detector-defined controls screen v1 — entry-gate artifacts

**Terminal status: `ENTRY_GATE_UNRESOLVED — NATIVE_DISPATCH_AGREEMENT_NOT_ESTABLISHED`**

Production never started. **No development training, no held-out training, no
six-arm comparison, and ZERO images generated.** No scientific decision is
available or claimed; **CPR's detector-defined retention behaviour remains
untested.**

**The blocker.** The required gate — native path with loss dispatch
disabled/enabled must agree under controlled inputs/RNG — was frozen with an
**exact-equality** criterion on the trained native PEFT adapter hash. It
failed (`c05be7b1…` vs `ed373817…`). The patch is inert by code inspection and
deterministic algorithms were never enabled, so GPU non-determinism is the
likely cause — **but that was not verified**: the OFF-vs-OFF control was not
run, because the single technical GPU retry was already spent and loosening a
frozen criterion after seeing the outcome is forbidden. This is a
gate-specification defect.

**What passed first:** categories by metadata alone (dev `stop sign`; held-out
`bench`, `fire hydrant`); **both evaluators QUALIFIED, 7/7 classes** at
≥16/20 positives and negatives; CPU implementation gate 64 rows / 0 failures;
native GEM + **native PEFT** bring-up (76 `qk_dual` modules, base frozen,
save/reload); budget projected 8.16 of 16 usable GPU-hours.

Report: [`FINAL_REPORT.md`](https://github.com/bijay299/XXResearch/blob/00bc8ae0a3d98640cb49cbbe616d2101e827e64f/results/cpr_detector_controls_v1/FINAL_REPORT.md)

name: Task B — matched-pair comparison (THR-V1-B)
body:
# Task B — matched-pair comparison (`THR-V1-B`)

Second-stage questionnaire for the **same two reviewers who completed Task A**.
20 matched pairs, offline, about 15–25 minutes.

> ## ⚠️ This stage is partially unmasked — by design
>
> Every pair **tells you which image is which**: one is labelled **REFERENCE**
> (the original model's output), the other **CANDIDATE** (the modified model's
> output). The comparison requires it.
>
> This release therefore **does not conceal matched pairs or condition roles**.
> Because the 40 images are already public in
> [`modern-object-assets-v1`](https://github.com/bijay299/XXResearch/releases/tag/modern-object-assets-v1),
> it **can enable matching back to the public Task-A images**, even though no
> crosswalk is published.
>
> **Publishing here does not restrict access to any particular people.** Anyone
> can download this. **Eligibility is procedural**: the intended primary cohort
> is exactly the two reviewers who completed Task A, and extra public downloads
> or returns are **not** automatically eligible.

## Status

Task A is **closed** with **2** independent reviewers (planned 3; the frozen
minimum is ≥2). This release reports **no outcome, no label and no image
judgement** — none exists.

## How to use it

1. Download and **fully extract** the ZIP.
2. Open `index.html` from the extracted folder.

Entirely offline — no account, no login, no upload, no tracking, no network.
Answers stay in the reviewer's browser until they export a JSON file.

**Please leave your Task A answers exactly as you submitted them.** This viewer
cannot read or alter them, and it refuses Task A files.

## The question

For each of 20 pairs:

> Does the candidate show **less**, **about the same**, or **more** structural
> deformation than the reference — or can you **not fairly compare** them?

plus an optional explanation. "Cannot fairly compare" is a **completed answer**.
Each image renders at native 512×512 and **zooms independently** of the other.

The instructions state plainly that the reference may already contain defects,
and that a changed layout, a coherent substitution or a missing teapot is **not
automatically deterioration** — matched initial noise does not guarantee
identical composition.

## Verification

* Integrity `TASKB_INTEGRITY_VERIFIED` — 20/20 pairs, 40/40 images, 20/20 role
  assignments, 40/40 image hashes matching the approved source, 20/20 pairs with
  byte-identical initial noise.
* **174/174** synthetic browser checks across **three engine configurations**
  (Chromium, Firefox, strict-file-origin Firefox), offline with **0 network
  requests**.
* Bundle audit clean: no crosswalk, case IDs, seeds, prompts, source filenames,
  salt, Task-A data, reviewer roster, answer keys or test exports.

## Versions

`THR-V1-B` · protocol `TEAPOT-HR-PROTO-1.0.0` · schema
`THR-EXPORT-SCHEMA-1.1.0` · app `1.1.0` build `taskB-b1`. Legacy `1.0.0` exports
are rejected, not migrated.

All images are **AI-generated**, reused byte-unchanged under the terms recorded
in the `modern-object-assets-v1` release.

---

Full documentation and the amendment:
[`results/teapot_human_review_v1/`](https://github.com/bijay299/XXResearch/tree/898c5525d9bc3db71324914281243ba0d9ad4336/results/teapot_human_review_v1)

body:
# Task A — corrected reviewer bundle (`patch01`)

**Use this release.** It supersedes `teapot-human-review-v1-taskA`, which is
preserved for the record but **does not open in Chrome or Edge**.

> ## Status: `READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW` — Task A only
>
> The instrument is built, complete, masked, validated and browser-tested in
> three engine configurations. It does **not** establish that any participant
> exists, that any label has been collected, that the evaluation is
> scientifically valid, or that erasure succeeded.
>
> **No reviewer has been recruited or contacted. No response exists. No outcome
> is reported.**

## What changed

Five defects were found after the first publication and repaired:

1. **Would not open in Chrome or Edge** — the item list was fetched with
   `XMLHttpRequest` over `file://`, which Chromium browsers block by CORS
   policy. It now loads with a plain `<script src="items.js">`.
2. **Import validation was far too weak** — it checked almost nothing and then
   *merged* a file into whatever session was open, keeping that session's alias
   and declarations. Imports are now fully validated before anything is touched
   and **restore their own session**; they are never merged into another alias.
   A rejected import leaves memory and saved state unchanged.
3. **Completion counted truthiness**, not valid choices.
4. **The companion Python validator had a hard-coded host path.**
5. **A mis-stated QA claim** was withdrawn and a genuine Final re-import test
   added.

Also corrected: ordering-provenance claims, exposure wording (now "Before
starting this Task A review", covering same-day exposure), and the stated scope
of the published commitments.

**Nothing about the study material changed.** The 40 image bytes, neutral IDs,
pairings, private mapping, fixed order permutations and published commitments
are unchanged and verified identical.

## Using it

1. Download and **fully extract** the ZIP.
2. Open `index.html` from the extracted folder.

Entirely offline — no account, no upload, no tracking, no network. Answers stay
in the reviewer's browser until they export a JSON file.

**Moving to another computer?** Export a draft, then on the new machine use
**"Continue from an exported file"** on the first screen. It restores that
file's own alias, declarations, order and answers.

## Scope and limits

* Export schema `THR-EXPORT-SCHEMA-1.1.0`, app `1.1.0`. Legacy `1.0.0` exports
  are **rejected, not migrated** — none exist.
* **Task B is not in this release** and is not published. The ZIP contains no
  Task-B content, pair association, mapping, answer key or test response.
* The underlying images and their condition/pair provenance are **already
  public**; neutral IDs reduce accidental disclosure but **cannot guarantee
  blinding**.
* All images are **AI-generated**, reused byte-unchanged under the terms
  recorded in the `modern-object-assets-v1` release.

---

Full documentation and the amendment:
[`results/teapot_human_review_v1/`](https://github.com/bijay299/XXResearch/tree/ce3b95f1cf72bf6260f4210bcbc0649ebeb0ab3a/results/teapot_human_review_v1)

Offline reviewer bundle for **40 individual images**. Preparation only.

> This means the package is built, complete, masked, validated and
> browser-tested. It does **not** establish that any participant exists, that
> any independent label has been collected, that the evaluation is
> scientifically valid, or that erasure succeeded.
>

## What's here

| asset | what |
|---|---|
| `teapot-human-review-v1-taskA.zip` | the offline reviewer bundle — viewer + **40 images** + instructions |
| `preview_A1_instructions.png`, `preview_A3_mobile_instructions.png` | real UI screenshots of the instructions |
| `preview_A2_item_view_synthetic.png`, `preview_A4_mobile_item_synthetic.png` | item-view layout rendered against a **synthetic placeholder** — never a research image |

**ZIP:** 13,917,868 bytes, sha256
`45e3eb7aeb9443e35a4ab990969eb9aa450e2f36b2238192244050b320dbd005`,
46 members, 40 PNGs. The build is deterministic.

1. Download and **fully extract** the ZIP.
2. Open `index.html` from the extracted folder.

It runs **entirely offline** — no account, no login, no upload, no tracking, no

export a JSON file. Verified in a real browser with every non-`file://` request
aborted.

## What reviewers do

Each of 40 images is shown **alone**, at native 512×512 with zoom, under a
neutral opaque ID. Two required questions plus an optional reason:

1. **Target** — present / absent / uncertain
2. **Rendering** — coherent (at most ordinary small defects) / localized

No pairing, counterpart link, condition, filename, prompt, seed, machine score

The underlying images and their condition/pair provenance are **already public**

**cannot prevent reverse matching and do not guarantee blinding**. Nothing here

Task-B content, no pair association, no mapping and no answer key.

All images are **AI-generated** outputs of FLUX.1-dev and of a GEM fine-tuned

body:
# modern_object_assets_v1 — GEM / FLUX.1-dev `teapot`

Actual trained checkpoint artifacts and 20 matched original/edited image pairs.

**Infrastructure milestone, not a method or paper contribution.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Method | GEM — `multimodal-ai-lab/GEM` @ `c328fc6bec687efe60223498d1b6bed2e5fbcffd` (MIT) |
| Backbone | `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev` @ `3de623fc3c33e44ffbe2bad470d0f45bccf2eb21` (gated) |
| Target / anchor | `teapot` / `""` (the source default `EMPTY_CONCEPT`) |
| Precision / resolution | bfloat16 / 512×512 |
| Trainable | native GEM LoRA, `qk_dual`, r16 α16 drop0.1 — 7,471,104 params across 76 modules |
| Training | 250 processed timesteps (the source's own counter) = 23 optimizer updates; native stop at `global_step 22` |

## ⚠️ What is and is not established

**Delivered (technical).** Exactly **76** transformer tensors changed from
pristine M0 (the `qk_dual` targets, nothing else, over 1160 keys compared) — so
this is **not** a no-op checkpoint. All post-merge tensors finite. The canonical
post-merge state and the state reloaded from disk are
**`SAVE_RELOAD_BITWISE_IDENTICAL`**. 20/20 pairs complete at original 512×512
under **byte-identical initial-noise tensors**.

**Not assessed: erasure efficacy.** No detector-recognition, suppression,
retention or visual-quality threshold was applied. No automated judge was run and
no scientific human label was assigned. **A technically valid but ineffective
edit would be indistinguishable from this release.**

This is a **source-derived GEM configuration for an ordinary object** — *not* an
author-validated object benchmark and *not* a reproduction of paper performance.
No SOTA, novelty, evaluator-bias, human-consensus or paper-readiness claim is
made. Not endorsed or validated by Black Forest Labs Inc. or by the GEM authors.

## Assets

| asset | what |
|---|---|
| `gem-flux-teapot-v1-transformer.tar.part000` … `part022` | **the native merged transformer** (GEM's own saved representation), 23 lossless 1 GiB parts |
| `gem-flux-teapot-v1-lora-adapter.tar.gz` | pre-merge native PEFT LoRA adapter (27.6 MiB) |
| `gem-flux-teapot-v1-images.tar.gz` | **all 40 primary PNGs** at original resolution + contact sheet + per-case indices + the 20 initial-noise tensors |
| `gem-flux-teapot-v1-contact-sheet.png` | contact sheet, standalone |
| `gem-flux-teapot-v1-evidence.tar.gz` | configs, manifests, per-key digests, patches, ledger, native logs |
| `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` | **complete per-part and reconstructed-file sha256 index** |
| `NOTICE.txt` | required attribution, modification statement, AI-generated-image disclosure |
| `FLUX.1-dev_LICENSE.md`, `GEM_LICENSE_MIT.txt` | required licence copies |

### Reconstructing the checkpoint

```bash
cat gem-flux-teapot-v1-transformer.tar.part* > gem-flux-teapot-v1-transformer.tar
sha256sum gem-flux-teapot-v1-transformer.tar
# expect 32d8202d0bdae63674fb7ea9a530f1b13df5acfbf831526c764e12deb1c6381d
tar -xf gem-flux-teapot-v1-transformer.tar     # -> transformer/
```

Load it through GEM's documented path: `PipelineConfig.default_for_model_type('flux')`
with `model_dtype='bfloat16'` and `model_name_or_path=<dir containing transformer/>`,
which makes `overwrite_pipeline_components_from_directory` replace the `transformer`
component against the pinned base.

**Measured:** the 27.6 MiB LoRA adapter, re-merged onto the pinned base via GEM's
own `merge_and_unload_all_adapters`, reproduces this endpoint **bitwise-identically**
(0 of 1160 tensors differ). Either route works. Nothing was quantized or cast to fit
hosting; the parts are a lossless split (GitHub caps each asset at 2 GiB).

## Requirements

* **Gated base access** to `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev` at revision
  `3de623fc3c33e44ffbe2bad470d0f45bccf2eb21` (accept the licence on Hugging Face).
  Pristine base weights are **not** republished here.
* Python ≥ 3.11, the locked environment (torch 2.9.1+cu128, diffusers 0.37.1,
  transformers 5.8.1, peft 0.19.1), the pinned GEM source, and a ≥ 40 GB GPU for
  512×512 bfloat16 inference as configured.

## Licence

The trained transformer is a **Derivative of the FLUX.1 [dev] Model** and is
distributed under the **FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License v1.1.1** for
**Non-Commercial Purposes only**. Rights are granted directly by Black Forest Labs
Inc. to you under that licence; a full copy ships with this release. The GEM source
code's MIT licence does **not** relicense these FLUX-derived weights.

**All 40 images were generated by an artificial-intelligence model.** They are not
photographs and do not depict real objects, places, people or events.

See `NOTICE.txt` for the complete required notices.

---
